authors: Marc Jourdan, Degenne Rémy, Kaufmann Emilie

context: While the literature abounds with designs of sampling rule, the optimal calibration of stopping rules is a most pressing issue as it leads to lower empirical stopping time. While calibrated thresholds have been derived with (near) optimal dependency in δ, those thresholds are known to be too conservative in the moderate confidence regime where their empirical error rate is orders of magnitude lower than δ. Finally, in the fixed-budget setting, characterizing the impact of not knowing the variances on the probability of misidentifying the best-arm is still an open problem.
